audit.whatIsWrong: Stored chart (Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo, Skill, Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo) disagrees with the mirror.
audit.why: The mirror audit set Level 1 Skill, Level 2 Gragas, Level 3 Skill, Levels 4-5 Gragas, Level 6 Gragas, First item Yasuo, 2+ items Yasuo as one atomic group across both layers. Matching it keeps the two directions from rendering opposite answers. whys[1..4] rewritten to agree.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 4 flipped in both layers with ratings rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns despite the whole page saying 'trade around Body Slam'.
audit.why: Barrel Roll 10/9/8/7/6, Drunken Rage 5s flat, Body Slam 14/13.5/13/12.5/12, Explosive Cask 100/85/70, Last Breath 70/50/30.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0], spikes[1], spikes[2], spikes[3], mid, phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Last Breath converts ANY knockup' is false here, and Drunken Rage's damage reduction plus auto reset were never mentioned.
audit.why: Explosive Cask knocks BACK, and Body Slam stuns — neither makes Gragas airborne, so Last Breath can only follow your own two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind, which the mirror states too. Drunken Rage is a 5s auto-attack reset that also reduces damage he takes: the wind-up is the burst tell, and it blunts your trade if you fight into it.
audit.corrected: Q2 whirlwind named as the only setup; Drunken Rage's reset and damage reduction written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears in the item list but is never tied to a mechanic.
audit.why: Happy Hour heals him periodically on every ability cast — Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[2].text, mid and breakdown.late.

edits.before: Level 2 stays Yasuo — his Body Slam trade leaves him on cooldown for you to punish.
edits.after: Level 2 goes to Gragas — Body Slam is 14s but his level-2 trade still out-damages yours.

edits.before: Level 3 goes to you as Wind Wall fully denies his primary Q poke pattern.
edits.after: Level 3 is even: Wind Wall denies Barrel Roll, but his E-Q burst matches it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 remain yours with Sweeping Blade weaving onto him after every E.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 go to Gragas as Drunken Rage cuts damage every 5 seconds.

edits.before: Level 6 is Yasuo's because your Last Breath punishes his gap-close before his ult matters in a duel.
edits.after: Level 6 favours Gragas — Explosive Cask hard-peels your dash and denies the knockup you need.

edits.before: Gragas leans on Barrel Roll (Q) poke and Body Slam (E) trades, but your Wind Wall eats the Q entirely and Sweeping Blade lets you weave onto him after he Body Slams in with E on cooldown.
edits.after: Gragas leans on Barrel Roll (Q, 10s at rank 1) and Body Slam (E, 14s). Drunken Rage (W) is a 5s auto reset that also cuts the damage he takes — the wind-up is your cue to step out, not the cast.

edits.before: Your R comes online before his ult matters in a duel — punish a Body Slam whiff or a Barrel Roll blocked by Wind Wall with a Q3 knock-up into Last Breath.
edits.after: Last Breath (70s at rank 1) needs YOUR Q2 whirlwind — his knockback never feeds it. Punish a Body Slam whiff: dash in, stack Q twice, whirlwind, then R.

edits.before: Crit plus your mobility means you win every extended trade; his only out is landing Explosive Cask (R) to peel your dash, so bait it before committing.
edits.after: Happy Hour heals him off every cast, so Executioner's Calling before your first item is what makes extended trades stick. Explosive Cask is 100s — bait it.

edits.before: Gragas becomes a utility bruiser who can't 1v1 you; respect only his flash-Cask disengage and Body Slam gap-close for ganks.
edits.after: Gragas becomes a utility bruiser who can't 1v1 you; respect only the flash-Cask disengage on a 70s late cooldown and his gank setup.

edits.before: Through Levels 3-6 your Sweeping Blade mobility and Q3 knock-up let you dictate every trade; a Body Slam whiff or a Wind-Walled Barrel Roll is a free burst window. Your R lands before his ult decides a duel, so you stay ahead the whole way.
edits.after: Through 3-6 Gragas edges the trades: Drunken Rage cuts your damage every 5s and Happy Hour heals him off each cast. Buy Grievous Wounds, punish the 14-second window after Body Slam, and never stand in the Barrel Roll pool.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Last Breath (70s at rank 1) fires only off your own Q2 whirlwind. Explosive Cask is 100s and knocks you away, not up.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window — build your teamfight around that. Gragas carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Last Breath needs an airborne target and only your own Q2 whirlwind supplies one. Gragas carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core against Happy Hour, shift to picks if he leads.

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gragas Body Slam: 14s at rank 1 — his engage and his escape, so trade in the gap after it. - Drunken Rage is 5s and cuts your damage. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: His engage. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His engage and escape, 14s at rank 1 — trade in the gap after it.
